title: Quasiparticle Interactions in the $S = 1/2$ Heisenberg Antiferromagnetic Chain CuPzN
authors: Leshan Zhao, Timothy Reeder, Matthew Stone, Daniel G. Mazzone, Jakob Lass, Christof Niedermayer, Daniel H. Reich, Anna Keselman, Oleg A. Starykh, Collin Broholm
abstract: We investigate spinon--spinon interactions in the quasi-one-dimensional $S=1/2$ Heisenberg antiferromagnet Cu(C$_4$H$_4$N$_2$)(NO$_3$)$_2$ (CuPzN) using inelastic neutron scattering. At zero field, the spectrum exhibits the canonical multi-spinon continuum of the Heisenberg chain. With increasing field we demonstrate the appearance of an energy gap $2Δ$ towards momentum $q\rightarrow 0$ between the uniform magnetization precession mode and the shifted spinon continuum. $2Δ$ is a direct measure of spinon backscattering interactions. Comparison with numerical matrix-product-state calculations and a recent analytical theory shows excellent agreement. By examining the integrable spin-1/2 chain, we provide an example of how quasiparticle interactions can be quantified experimentally in isotropic quantum spin systems.
summary: This research uses inelastic neutron scattering on a quasi-1D quantum magnet to study spinon-spinon interactions. By measuring the opening of an energy gap ($2\Delta$) as a magnetic field is applied, the authors provide a direct, quantitative measure of these interactions. The results strongly validate the theoretical understanding of spinon dynamics in integrable quantum spin chains.
main_problem: The paper investigates the nature and quantification of spinon-spinon interactions within a quasi-one-dimensional quantum magnet.
main_result: The authors experimentally measure an energy gap, $2\Delta$, at finite magnetic fields, which provides a direct and quantitative measure of the spinon backscattering interactions, showing excellent agreement with advanced theoretical calculations.
method: The study combines inelastic neutron scattering experiments on $	ext{CuPzN}$ with sophisticated theoretical modeling using Matrix-Product-State (MPS) calculations and analytical theory.
model_or_system: The system is the $S=1/2$ Heisenberg antiferromagnetic chain, realized in the material $	ext{Cu}(	ext{C}_4	ext{H}_4	ext{N}_2)(	ext{NO}_3)_2$ ($	ext{CuPzN}$). The analysis focuses on the spinon continuum and its modification by external magnetic fields.
key_observables: The energy gap $2\Delta$ at low momentum ($q 	o 0$), the spinon dispersion relations $\hbar\omega_{\pm}(	ilde{q})$, and the dynamical structure factor $S(	ilde{q}, \omega)$.
important_parameters: The magnetic field strength ($\mu_0H$), the exchange coupling constant ($J$), and the derived spinon backscattering strength ($g$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system can be modeled as an integrable spin-1/2 chain, and the measurements are projected onto the first Brillouin zone.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the measured and calculated dynamical structure factor $S(	ilde{q}, \omega)$ at zero and finite fields, highlighting the appearance of the $2\Delta$ energy gap. Other figures present extracted dispersion relations and comparisons of the gap magnitude versus magnetization.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first establishing the zero-field spinon continuum via neutron scattering. It then analyzes the field dependence, demonstrating the gap opening ($2\Delta$) as the key diagnostic tool. Finally, it quantitatively compares the measured gap and dispersion to MPS calculations and analytical theory to extract interaction parameters.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, measurable experimental realization of quantifying quasiparticle interactions (spinon interactions) in a strongly correlated quantum spin system, bridging experimental spectroscopy with advanced theoretical techniques like MPS.

Dynamical structure factor S(˜q, ω) of CuPzN mea- sured by neutron scattering at T = 50 mK in magnetic fields (a) µ0H = 0, (c) µ0H = 6.8 T, and (e) µ0H = 11 T applied along the c-axis, which is perpendicular to the a-oriented spin chain. (b, d, f) Corresponding dynamical structure factor Scal(˜q, ω), calculated using time-evolution block deci- mation (TEBD) from a matrix-product state (MPS) ground state obtained by the density-matrix...

FIG. 2. Dynamical structure factor S(˜q, ω) as a function of energy transfer ℏω at fixed momenta ˜q along the spin chain for CuPzN, measured at µ0H = 11 T. Curves at different ˜q are vertically offset by 0.015 meV−1 for clarity. Dashed lines show Scal(˜q, ω) calculated numerically, as described in text. Red stars indicate the centers of spinon dispersion peaks, ex- tracted from Gaussian fits to the measurements. Red lines show dispersion relations determined from the peak positions.

FIG. 3. Dispersion relations ℏω±(q) for collective spinon modes in CuPzN measured at (a) µ0H = 11 T and (b) µ0H = 6.8 T, extracted from Gaussian fits to constant-˜q cuts through S(˜q, ω). Dashed lines show fits to Eq. (3), from which the energy gap 2∆at ˜q = 0 was extracted. (c, d) Spectral weights S±(˜q) for the collective spinon modes measured at (c) µ0H = 11 T and (d) µ0H = 6.8 T. Dashed lines represent the spectral weights calculated using Eq. (2) with parameters listed in Table I.

FIG. 4. (a) Experimental (red) and calculated (black) energy gap 2∆between the uniform magnetization mode and the shifted spinon continuum at ˜q = 0 versus the relative mag- netization M/Msat, where Msat = 1/2 is the dimensionless saturation magnetization. The dashed line shows a quadratic fit to the measured data. The linear coefficient g represents contribution from two-spinon back-scattering interaction, and α accounts for higher order effects not captured in the analyt- ical theory [12]. (b) Normalized quantum Fisher information (nQFI) for CuPzN versus M/Msat, with red dots denoting experimental measurements and black dots numerical calcu- lations convolved with instrumental resolution.

FIG. 5. Two-spinon back-scattering interaction strength g as a function of the second-nearest-neighbor exchange inter- action J2/J. Black points show numerically calculated val- ues, and the red shaded region indicates the range within one standard deviation of the experimental measurement. A con- straint on the second-nearest-neighbor exchange in CuPzN of −0.04 < J2/J < 0.02 is found.
